title: Holding Government Contractors Accountable for Wrongdoing
summary: Argus Information and Advisory Services, a subsidiary of TransUnion, has agreed in writing that it will not seek any government contract with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau for three years.

title: Back from the Dead: Zombie Second Mortgages
summary: Forgotten second mortgages may be coming back to haunt homeowners who haven’t received notices or account statements for years.

title: Strengthening Appraisal Oversight: Progress at the Appraisal Subcommittee
summary: CFPB Deputy Director Zixta Martinez discusses changes at the ASC since she became Chair in 2022, including enhanced state oversight, landmark hearings on appraisal bias, and improved collaboration with The Appraisal Foundation to create a more equitable and accountable appraisal industry.

title: Holding Credit Reporting Companies Accountable for Junk Data
summary: Including junk data and mistakes on people's credit reports is against the law.

title: What We’re Watching: Language Access in Consumer Finance
summary: Financial institutions are increasingly serving consumers in languages other than English.

title: Strengthening State-Level Consumer Protections
summary: Today, the CFPB is releasing new recommendations to states on how they can update their laws and regulations to meet new risks and challenges.

title: New protections for payday and installment loans take effect March 30
summary: The CFPB’s rule protecting payday and installment loan borrowers takes effect on March 30, 2025.

title: LFG (Looking for gamers): CFPB wants to hear about your video game loot
summary: The CFPB invites video gamers to share their experiences with video game currencies, gaming companies, fraud, scams, and account hacks.

title: Protecting you from unlawful debt collection at work
summary: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau is stopping companies from improperly contacting people in the workplace to put pressure on them to pay allegedly owed debts.

title: New tactics from companies trying to charge illegal junk fees
summary: As companies are stopped from charging illegal junk fees, people are facing new risks as companies experiment with sketchy fee tactics, which are themselves also often illegal.

title: Los cheques de reembolsos de CreditRepair.com y Lexington Law: Lo que usted necesita saber
summary: Más de 4 millones de consumidores, quienes fueron perjudicados por las actividades ilegales de Lexington Law y CreditRepair.com. recibirán cheques de reembolso a partir de diciembre.

title: CreditRepair.com and Lexington Law refund checks: What you need to know
summary: Over 4 million consumers harmed by Lexington Law and CreditRepair.com’s illegal credit repair activities will receive refund checks beginning in December.

title: CFPB Ombudsman’s Office 2024 Annual Report
summary: The CFPB Ombudsman’s Office shares its FY2024 Annual Report

title: CFPB distribuirá más de $191 millones a los consumidores perjudicados por Tempoe
summary: Este octubre, más de 250.000 consumidores que fueron perjudicados por la compañía de arrendamientos Tempoe, LLC, comenzarán a recibir cheques por correo. Tempoe engañó a los clientes de grandes comercios para que tomaran costosos contratos de arrendamiento.

title: CFPB to distribute over $191 million to consumers harmed by Tempoe
summary: In October, over 250,000 consumers harmed by leasing company Tempoe, LLC, will begin receiving refund checks in the mail. Tempoe tricked customers of major retailers into expensive lease agreements.

title: La Deuda Médica y las Prácticas de Facturación de los Hospitales sin Fines de Lucro
summary: Los hospitales sin fines de lucro deben ofrecer asistencia financiera. Muchos consumidores no reciben esta asistencia, o son acosados por cobradores.

title: Medical Debt and Non-Profit Hospital Billing Practices
summary: Millions of consumers seek urgent medical care at non-profit hospitals that are required to provide financial assistance to patients in need. However, many eligible consumers either don’t receive this financial assistance or are pursued by debt collectors for bills they don’t owe.

title: CFPB launches public comment process for open banking standard setter recognition
summary: The public can submit comments on open banking standard-setter applications to ensure the development of fair and effective open banking standards that serve the interests of all stakeholders, especially consumers.

title: Debt collectors that take advantage of surviving spouses and their vulnerabilities
summary: The CFPB is concerned that medical debt collectors may try to capitalize on surviving spouses’ vulnerabilities to try to collect unpaid medical bills, including bills that may not even be owed.

title: High Interest Rates Set to Increase the Cost of Student Loans in 2024
summary: Higher student loan interest rates could cost students over $3 billion in additional interest for loans taken out in this year alone.

title: Promoting competition in payments
summary: Director Chopra reacts to Apple’s recent announcement about planned changes to “tap-to-pay” functionality on its iOS devices.

title: Preserving free access to money in your account
summary: The CFPB has found that people are paying more for their cash, not only at out-of-network ATMs, but also at places like grocery stores and retailers that previously provided access for free.

title: What we're learning: Medical debt's impact on Alaska Native communities
summary: There is a disproportionate impact of medical debt on American Indian and Alaska Native consumers, in Alaska and across the United States.

title: What Buy Now, Pay Later lenders are doing to be upfront with borrowers
summary: The CFPB has received feedback on its BNPL interpretive rule and will now provide more clarity and guidance on company compliance and the benefits to consumers.

title: Recover financially from floods, and take steps for the rest of the storm season
summary: Tropical Storm Debby caused heavy flooding all over the eastern part of the country. We have tips to help you get back on your feet financially and prepare for an active storm season.
